events.summary: Colombo’s 50,000-family housing deed programme is scheduled to begin in February.
Semata Nivahana plans to provide 15,000 housing loans by early March.
Six additional wind turbines are planned at an estimated cost of $47 million.
Sri Lanka and Maldives agreed to start an air ambulance service in March.
Ten thousand Urumaya land deeds were completed and sent to divisional secretariats.
Cabinet approved vehicle imports for the Ports, Shipping and Education Ministries.
Three agreements with China were signed for youth vocational training.
Cabinet authorised procedures to export rocks removed during Hambantota port construction.
Cabinet approved six wind turbines on Mannar Island using ADB financing.
Cabinet approved private investors to implement the Mannar wind project.
UNDP-funded incinerator construction at Jaffna Teaching Hospital is nearing completion.
India invited applications for about 200 fully funded Sri Lankan student scholarships.
Government spent about Rs. 22 billion on fertilizer purchase subsidies in 2023.
Government spent Rs. 13 billion purchasing rice in 2023.
Government allocated Rs. 1 billion for drought-related crop damage compensation.
Government had already paid Rs. 700 million in drought crop compensation.
Government began subsidised fertilizer distribution for tea cultivation.
Sri Lanka prioritized four crops to reach national consumption targets in 2024.
Eastern Governor arranged a 30-year land lease and lease payment for the college.
Education Ministry extended school shoe voucher validity to 17 February 2024.
India-Sri Lanka passenger ferry service planned to resume on 15 February.
President directed monthly A/L scholarship payments to increase to Rs. 6,000.
Litro Gas handed Rs. 1.5 billion profit to the Treasury.
Government proposed leasing state plantations for cocoa cultivation.
President proposed creating investment zones nationwide to expand the economy.
Authorities pursued appointments for 22,000 graduates amid teacher shortages.
Recruitment process for 5,500 teachers began after a gazette notification.
Sri Lanka planned talks with a Chinese company on a Northern fisheries investment zone.
Fisherfolk welfare service planned to provide emergency health services at sea.
Ten billion rupees was allocated for regional development activities.
Rotary clubs handed critical-care equipment to Colombo National Hospital.
Steps were underway to appoint 22,000 graduate teachers, pending court proceedings.
Health minister requested UNDP support for modern medical and dengue-control equipment.
Government plans to use national identity numbers as taxpayer identification numbers.
Cabinet paper seeks approval to implement title deeds for 50,000 urban housing units.
Police launched a Colombo pilot using CCTV to monitor traffic violations.
Vocational training will begin for A/L students in 299 selected schools.
Government planned a nationwide network of VAT-free shops after a feasibility study.
CEB submitted a proposal to revise electricity tariffs for regulatory public consultation.
Education Ministry announced a nationwide vocational guidance programme for A-level students.
Police announced a nationwide school drug-prevention awareness programme beginning February 5.
Sri Lanka completed initial steps toward issuing electronic passports.
Government will invite new Aswesuma applications in February’s first week.
Government decided to add 300,000 families to Aswesuma welfare payments.
Health Ministry planned catch-up vaccinations for unvaccinated children.
Immigration Department completed the e-passport programme’s initial phase.
Procurement for electronic passports was underway.
Agriculture Ministry planned a Cabinet paper on subsidised electricity for Jaffna farmers.
Yala National Park's main entrance reopened after flood damage repairs.
CEB submitted a tariff revision proposal to the utilities regulator.
Russia donated US$1.5 million of sunflower oil through the World Food Programme.
An interim guidance committee for tuk-tuk drivers was established.
Minister considered introducing QR registration for tuk-tuk drivers.
Supplementary allocation approved for presidential foreign travel expenses
Interim steering committee established for three-wheeler drivers' trade unions.
Armed forces mobilized to support nationwide hospital operations during a health worker strike.
Government authorised essential vehicle imports for ministries under foreign-funded projects.
